author: Admilson B. F. Cossa
authority: runtime source and npm run verify

claims.title: run.race cancels losing branches
claims.expectedInvariant: losing branches receive race_lost cancellation
claims.limitations: Provider billing or remote execution stops only when the underlying provider honors AbortSignal.

claims.title: run.retry stops on parent cancellation
claims.expectedInvariant: no extra retry attempt runs after cancellation is observed
claims.limitations: The guarantee applies to WorkIt retry sleeps and task bodies that observe ctx.signal.

claims.title: run.bracket cleanup timeout is bounded and observable
claims.expectedInvariant: a hanging cleanup emits task:cleanup_timeout and the owner settles
claims.limitations: The timeout bounds WorkIt cleanup waiting; external systems still need their own timeout and idempotency policies.

claims.title: replay receipts record completed scope closure
claims.expectedInvariant: a closed successful scope has completed terminal outcome and no leaked tasks
claims.limitations: Receipts are audit evidence over observed WorkIt events and snapshots; they are not deterministic scheduler replay.

claims.title: replay receipts preserve typed cancellation reason
claims.expectedInvariant: a manually cancelled scope records the cancellation reason observed by owned work
claims.limitations: The reason is evidence captured from WorkIt-owned cancellation; external systems still need their own abort support.

claims.title: shared scope resource acquires and releases once
claims.expectedInvariant: parallel tasks using one shared helper observe one acquisition and one scope-owned release
claims.limitations: This proves WorkIt helper ownership and cleanup registration; external resource semantics remain application responsibility.

claims.title: file activity store replays completed activity after restart
claims.expectedInvariant: a fresh file activity store returns the persisted terminal result without rerunning the activity body
claims.limitations: This is terminal activity replay for explicit activity ids; it is not arbitrary in-flight crash recovery or workflow replay.

claims.title: resource ownership can be audited across cleanup paths
claims.expectedInvariant: explicit resource audit instrumentation records acquired/released/pending resources while WorkIt emits cleanup timeout and failure events
claims.limitations: Resource audit entries are explicit caller instrumentation; WorkIt supplies cleanup failure and timeout events through the scope event surface.

claims.title: budget inputs are immutable boundary values
claims.expectedInvariant: caller input object is not mutated; final spent value is read from run.context.budget
claims.limitations: Applications must read runtime budget state through the context API rather than expecting mutation of the original object.

claims.title: channel capacity applies producer backpressure
claims.expectedInvariant: third send to capacity-two channel blocks until a receive drains one item
claims.limitations: This proof covers local channel capacity, not distributed queue semantics.

claims.title: diagnostics report stable cleanup finding codes
claims.expectedInvariant: cleanup timeout events produce cleanup_timeout findings
claims.limitations: Rich rendering and exporter behavior are separate optional surfaces.

claims.title: retry policy rejects unsafe attempt counts
claims.expectedInvariant: unbounded retry counts are rejected at the policy boundary
claims.limitations: The cap prevents accidental huge retry policies; application-level retry budgets may be stricter.

claims.title: receipt analysis detects leaked owned work
claims.expectedInvariant: a non-terminal receipt with pending tasks fails analysis with leaked_tasks
claims.limitations: The verifier analyzes receipt evidence supplied to it; it does not observe work that was never captured.

claims.title: explicit activity boundary preserves terminal evidence
claims.expectedInvariant: completed activity returns the stored result on repeat and changed input conflicts before rerun
claims.limitations: The boundary records explicit terminal activity evidence; callers remain responsible for idempotent external side effects.

claims.title: receipt verifier proves declared lifecycle evidence
claims.expectedInvariant: a closed receipt with terminal and cleanup evidence verifies no orphaned owned tasks while preserving cleanup timeout warning evidence
claims.limitations: Verification is bounded to the receipt and snapshot supplied by the caller.

claims.title: bounded resource model preserves cleanup balance invariant
claims.expectedInvariant: for linear, lazy, and shared resources, every terminal modeled scope releases exactly the resources it acquired
claims.limitations: This is a bounded model for WorkIt resource helper contracts, not a proof over arbitrary JavaScript programs or external resources.

claims.title: source protocol analysis detects missing ownership edges
claims.expectedInvariant: bounded source protocol specs pass when WorkIt ownership edges are present and fail with stable findings when ownership edges are missing
claims.limitations: This verifies caller-provided protocol specifications, not arbitrary TypeScript or JavaScript source.

claims.title: worker offload rejects remote and executable URL schemes
claims.expectedInvariant: data, http, https, and javascript worker inputs are rejected before import
claims.limitations: Local file URLs remain application authority; WorkIt does not sandbox arbitrary trusted local code.

claims.title: worker timeout terminates non-cooperative CPU work
claims.expectedInvariant: late marker is not written after offload timeout
claims.limitations: The hard boundary applies to worker offload; JavaScript cannot preempt a CPU loop on the main thread.

claims.title: public proof artifact exposes release evidence
claims.expectedInvariant: benchmarks/public-proof.json exposes commands, fixtures, guides, and runtime matrix
claims.limitations: This verifies repository artifact shape, not an external registry publication event.

claims.title: release policy documents signed tags and worker boundary
claims.expectedInvariant: SECURITY.md documents signed tags and structured-clone worker input
claims.limitations: Documentation must remain aligned with the actual release workflow.

claims.title: release provenance gate verifies tag policy
claims.expectedInvariant: release-provenance script contains signed-tag verification logic
claims.limitations: A dry-run gate cannot guarantee a future maintainer will sign a tag; it verifies that the repository policy gate exists.

claims.title: file receipt ledger persists append-only receipt evidence
claims.expectedInvariant: a receipt appended by one ledger instance is readable from a new ledger instance
claims.limitations: This proof covers WorkIt's file-backed receipt ledger, not database durability or distributed queue semantics.

claims.title: article benchmark suite has expected executable coverage
claims.expectedInvariant: benchmarks/articles contains exactly 19 numbered benchmark scripts
claims.limitations: Coverage count does not prove a benchmark result; individual benchmark assertions do.

claims.title: captured article benchmark result is machine-readable
claims.expectedInvariant: benchmarks/results/articles.latest.json records 19 passing benches
claims.limitations: Timing values are representative for the captured machine and run; semantic assertions are the portable claim.
